first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A Portugal wedding guide that also sells a planning service: pick a region, check the legal steps for our passport, then talk to one 'Wedded Advisor'. The headline sells palaces and cliffs, but it reads more like a destination guide than a full-service destination wedding planner showing me what they have done.

attention_map.quote: Wedded Concierge plans weddings in Portugal for couples from Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom, with one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: One point of contact the whole way through is exactly what we want, and it names the US and UK, so it is not just for Australians. The legal quick answer is useful. But 'Wedded Advisor' tells me nothing about how senior that person is.

attention_map.quote: a non-numeric line naming Wedded Concierge and one Wedded Advisor, or hide the strip
attention_map.why: This is where I look for proof before I scroll any further. If it is blank or just repeats the service name, there is nothing here: no press, no numbers, no faces.
Fine, but I would not hand over details this early when I have no idea who is on the other end.

attention_map.quote: a ceremony in a Sintra national palace or park booked through Parques de Sintra, then a Douro day for guests
attention_map.why: Nice enough, but it is tourism-board material. Any guide I have open in another tab says the same.

attention_map.quote: Setting; Best months; Nearest airport (code); Guests
attention_map.why: An airport on every card is what I came for. But I only get airport codes, no drive times, and Guests is blank or says 'Ask your Wedded Advisor'. 'within two hours of an airport' is still a guess for the Douro and Comporta.

attention_map.quote: Monserrate roof restoration with scaffolding and a temporary covering runs until Q1 2027
attention_map.why: This is the first thing that sounds like someone who knows the ground. Telling me about state-event cancellations and scaffolding before I book is what a good planner does.

attention_map.quote: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee
attention_map.why: Useful and honest about how supplier costs work. It is all 'can', 'often', 'may', though, so it reads second-hand rather than from people who book these venues.

attention_map.section: s5-plan (Marrying legally by passport, Entry rules)
attention_map.quote: US passport: the US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI; you sign a statement of eligibility to marry before a consular officer
attention_map.why: Splitting the rules for US and UK passports is genuinely helpful, and the 'checked October 2026' line adds trust. That said, I expect our planner to deal with this for us, so I would skim it.

attention_map.quote: Fallback until then: explain what drives cost (guest count, region, season, nights at the venue, exclusivity) with no figures
attention_map.why: If it launches on the fallback, I get a list of cost drivers and no numbers. Even the signed-off version gives a EUR 25,000 to 70,000 range for 100 guests, which is far below what we are planning, and tells me nothing about what this firm charges.

attention_map.quote: Venue nights with rooms, welcome dinner, ceremony, long dinner, late party, Sunday brunch, an on-the-day coordinator.
attention_map.why: This is the nearest the page comes to describing a guest experience. But it lists what a weekend 'can include', not what the firm does. An 'on-the-day coordinator' sounds like a coordination package, not a full-service planner.

attention_map.quote: Guest website in Wonderland Studio with the button 'Start for free'.
attention_map.why: A free DIY guest website feels like it is aimed at a different, cheaper customer. It makes the brand feel less high end.

attention_map.quote: hidden at launch: only 2 Portugal real weddings
attention_map.why: This is the deal-breaker. I check proof before I go near the form. No Portugal weddings at all, while the other firms I am comparing open with their portfolio.

attention_map.quote: otherwise say a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call
attention_map.why: Read plainly, that means 'we won't tell you how we charge until you call'. No founder, no names, and nothing on why I should book through them instead of the venue. 'Answer from approved service facts only' sounds like the answer will be thin.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links make this feel like a wedding magazine, not a senior planning firm.

attention_map.quote: Is a wedding in Portugal cheaper than at home?
attention_map.why: The FAQs cover legal steps and beaches. None asks what this firm actually does or how it charges, and those are the two questions I have.

questions_answered.question: What exactly does end-to-end include?
questions_answered.evidence: 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' and the s6 weekend list ('welcome dinner, ceremony, long dinner, late party, Sunday brunch, an on-the-day coordinator'). That is framed as what a weekend 'can include', not as the firm's scope. Supplier sourcing, design, guest logistics and travel are not set out, so the scope is still vague.

questions_answered.question: Why an Australian company for a wedding in Europe?
questions_answered.evidence: The brief says only 'couples from Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom' and bans any capability claim. It never explains why this firm, or what it knows about Portugal. The passport tabs listing Australia first are the only clue about where the firm is based.

questions_answered.question: How far is it from a major airport?
questions_answered.evidence: Every region card gives a 'Nearest airport (code)': LIS, FAO, OPO, FNC. No drive times, Comporta is 'LIS with no drive time', the Douro distance is not used, and the only time given is 'many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the centre', which is from the centre, not the airport.

questions_answered.question: How are fees and supplier costs structured, and in what currency?
questions_answered.evidence: How supplier costs work is explained well in the venue charges box (exclusivity, buy-out, per day or per guest minimums, check VAT), and the cost table would be in EUR with 'AUD, USD and GBP amounts vary with the exchange rate'. But the figures wait on sign-off, and the firm's own fee is 'a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call'. The firm's fee structure is not answered.

questions_answered.question: Can we see weddings you have done here?
questions_answered.evidence: 's8-real-weddings ... HIDDEN AT LAUNCH: only 2 Portugal real weddings'. A Europe strip or trending row shows instead, and the trending row is celebrity weddings, not theirs.

trust_signals_noticed: Rules by passport for US and UK, sourced from official sites
'Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab.'
Honest palace caveats: state-event cancellations and Monserrate scaffolding to Q1 2027
Venue charges box explaining exclusivity, buy-outs and checking VAT
One Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend
Honest that there is no package, just a planned weekend
turn_offs_noticed: Vague scope: what the firm does is never spelt out beyond 'what a weekend can include'
No senior planner names or faces, no press, no founder
Celebrity trending links and a 'Start for free' guest website make it feel mass market
Hedging everywhere ('can', 'often', 'may') reads as second-hand knowledge

emotional_response.detail: I learnt useful things about Portugal and felt the page was honest. I did not feel anyone here was invested in us, or that I knew who would be. There is no human, no story and no wedding they have done.

payload.decision_reason: The region cards with airports, the passport rules and the palace caveats are better than most guides, so I would keep the tab open. But I enquire when scope, proof and fees are clear and the firm feels senior. Here the real weddings are hidden, no planner is named, the fee waits for a call and it never says why an Australian firm should run our Portugal wedding. Next to the other planners I am comparing, it loses on proof.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Honestly, it is a good Portugal guide. The passport stuff and the Sintra palace warnings are things I did not know. But I am not hiring a guide, I am hiring a planner, and I can't see a single wedding they have done here or who would actually plan ours. 'Explains fees on the first call' tells me I won't find out what it costs without getting on a call. I'll bookmark it, but the firms with a Portugal portfolio and a named lead planner get our enquiry first.
